1.explanation: This minimal React example uses the Carbon Dropdown component from carbon-components-react. By setting both disabled={true} and tabIndex={-1} on the Dropdown, you can reproduce the reported issue: the wrapper listbox container correctly receives tabIndex -1, but the inner button element (ListBoxField) remains focusable with tabIndex 0. This demonstrates that disabled children did not inherit the parent tabIndex, causing a keyboard focus gap.
1.bug_scenario: When a Dropdown is rendered with disabled=true and tabIndex={-1}, the outer ListBox wrapper correctly has tabindex="-1", but its inner button element (the ListBoxField) still retains tabindex="0". This means that even though the control is disabled and should not be focusable, keyboard users can still tab into the hidden inner control.
